records.source: וַיָּבִ֨יאוּ֙ אֶת־אֲר֣וֹן הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים וַיַּצִּ֣יגוּ אֹת֔וֹ בְּת֣וֹךְ הָאֹ֔הֶל אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָֽטָה־ל֖וֹ דָּוִ֑יד וַיַּקְרִ֛יבוּ עֹל֥וֹת וּשְׁלָמִ֖ים לִפְנֵ֥י הָאֱלֹהִֽים׃
records.gloss: And they brought [the] ark of the God and set it in [the] midst of the tent that pitched for it David; and they offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before the God.
pieces: They carried the ark of God in and set it within the tent David had pitched for it. Then they offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before God.

L.1: And they brought in the ark of God and set it inside the tent that David had pitched for it; and they offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before God.

R.1: They brought the ark of God into the tent David had set up for it. Then they offered burnt offerings and peace offerings to God.

decisions.choice: the same event as 2 Samuel 6:17, with small differences
decisions.reason: Verses 1-3 retell 2 Samuel 6:17-19, and their wording follows that passage wherever the Hebrew is the same. Here the ark is "the ark of God" (Samuel: "the ark of the LORD"); Samuel's "in its place" is not repeated; "they offered" stands where Samuel has "David offered"; and the offerings are made "before God" where Samuel has "before the LORD". Chronicles has just told how the Levites carried the ark up to Jerusalem (15:25-29), so "they" are the Levites and the people with David.

decisions.choice: the tent David had pitched: a new tent in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: This is the tent David set up for the ark in his city (15:1), not the old tabernacle, which verse 39 places at Gibeon. The ark stays in this tent until Solomon builds the temple.

A burnt offering was burned whole on the altar as a gift to God (Leviticus 1). Most of a peace offering was eaten by the worshipers in a shared meal (Leviticus 3; 7:11-15), which explains the food given out in verse 3.
With the article, "the God" is a common way of naming Israel's God in Chronicles (13:5-8); it means the one true God.

decisions.choice: offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before God (B); to God (R)
decisions.reason: As at 2 Samuel 6:17, Readable says "to God" for "before God"; it also leaves out "set it there", which is already said by bringing it into the tent.

records.heading: The ark in its tent

records.source: וַיְכַ֣ל דָּוִ֔יד מֵהַעֲל֥וֹת הָעֹלָ֖ה וְהַשְּׁלָמִ֑ים וַיְבָ֥רֶךְ אֶת־הָעָ֖ם בְּשֵׁ֥ם יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And finished David from offering up the burnt offering and the peace offerings, and he blessed the people in [the] name of Yahweh.
pieces: When David had finished offering the burnt offerings and the peace offerings, he pronounced a blessing on the people in the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.2: And David finished offering the burnt offering and the peace offerings, and he blessed the people in the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.2: When David was done with the burnt offerings and peace offerings, he spoke a blessing over the people in the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.reason: The verse is the same as 2 Samuel 6:18 except that Samuel calls God "the LORD of hosts" and Chronicles says only "the LORD".

decisions.choice: the burnt offering: all the burnt offerings
decisions.reason: The singular stands for the whole group of burnt offerings named in verse 1.

decisions.choice: blessed the people in the name of the LORD
decisions.reason: To bless in the LORD's name is to call down his good on people, speaking for him (Numbers 6:23-27). David does this as the king who leads the worship, as Solomon does when the temple is dedicated (2 Chronicles 6:3).

records.source: וַיְחַלֵּק֙ לְכָל־אִ֣ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מֵאִ֖ישׁ וְעַד־אִשָּׁ֑ה לְאִישׁ֙ כִּכַּר־לֶ֔חֶם וְאֶשְׁפָּ֖ר וַאֲשִׁישָֽׁה׃
records.gloss: And he distributed to every man of Israel, from man and to woman, to each [a] round-loaf of bread and [a] date-cake and [a] raisin-cake.
pieces: He also handed out food to every person in Israel, both men and women: a loaf of bread, a cake of dates and a cake of raisins for each one.

L.3: And he distributed to every person of Israel, from man to woman, to each a round loaf of bread and a date cake and a raisin cake.

R.3: He gave food to every person in Israel, both men and women. Each one received a loaf of bread, a cake of dates and a cake of raisins.

decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 6:19 reads "to all the people, to all the crowd of Israel" where this verse has "to every person of Israel"; it names a "cake" of bread where this verse has a "round loaf", and it says "one" with each item. The rest of 2 Samuel 6:19, the people going home, comes at the end of the chapter (verse 43), after the account of the Levites' worship.

decisions.choice: every person, from man to woman: men and women alike
decisions.reason: The word for "person" ('ish) is the ordinary word for a man, but "from man to woman" shows that the women were given a share too. The meal belonged with the peace offerings (verse 1), a feast of joy before God.

decisions.choice: a round loaf; a raisin cake
decisions.reason: The loaf (kikkar) is a round flat bread. The raisin cake was made of pressed dried grapes and was festival food (Hosea 3:1; Song of Songs 2:5).

The word is found only here and in 2 Samuel 6:19, and its meaning is not known for certain. It may be a cake of dates, or a portion of meat from the sacrifices; older guesses include a measure of wine.
Balanced and Readable say what was handed out before listing it, as at 2 Samuel 6:19.

records.source: וַיִּתֵּ֞ן לִפְנֵ֨י אֲר֧וֹן יְהוָ֛ה מִן־הַלְוִיִּ֖ם מְשָׁרְתִ֑ים וּלְהַזְכִּיר֙ וּלְהוֹד֣וֹת וּלְהַלֵּ֔ל לַיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃פ
records.gloss: And he appointed before [the] ark of Yahweh from the Levites ministering [ones], and to invoke and to give thanks and to praise Yahweh, [the] God of Israel.
pieces: He appointed some of the Levites to serve before the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, to invoke, to thank and to praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel.

L.4: And he appointed some of the Levites [as] ministers before the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, both to invoke and to give thanks and to praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel.

R.4: David chose some of the Levites to serve in front of the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Their work was to call on {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, and to thank {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: ministers: those who serve in worship
decisions.reason: The word (mesharet) is used of priests and Levites who serve the LORD at his sanctuary (Numbers 3:6; Deuteronomy 10:8). Now that the ark has a resting place and no longer has to be carried, the Levites are given a new service of song before it (6:16-17; 23:26-30).

decisions.choice: to invoke: to call on God by name, or to bring to remembrance
decisions.reason: The verb (hizkir) is "cause to remember". It can mean to call on God and mention his name in praise and prayer (Exodus 20:24; Isaiah 26:13), and it is used in the titles of two psalms that plead with God (Psalms 38:1; 70:1). It may also mean to bring God's deeds to mind in celebration. The song that follows does both: it calls on God and tells people to remember his works (verses 8, 12, 15).

decisions.choice: three parts of the Levites' worship
decisions.reason: The three verbs, to invoke, to give thanks and to praise, describe one service of worship. Giving thanks comes first in the song itself (verse 8) and returns at its close (verses 34-35).
Readable names David as the one who appointed the Levites and says "call on" for "invoke" (m2).

records.source: אָסָ֥ף הָרֹ֖אשׁ וּמִשְׁנֵ֣הוּ זְכַרְיָ֑ה יְעִיאֵ֡ל וּשְׁמִֽירָמ֡וֹת וִֽיחִיאֵ֡ל וּמַתִּתְיָ֡ה וֶאֱלִיאָ֡ב וּבְנָיָהוּ֩ וְעֹבֵ֨ד אֱדֹ֜ם וִֽיעִיאֵ֗ל בִּכְלֵ֤י נְבָלִים֙ וּבְכִנֹּר֔וֹת וְאָסָ֖ף בַּֽמְצִלְתַּ֥יִם מַשְׁמִֽיעַ׃
records.gloss: Asaph [was] the chief, and his second Zechariah; Jeiel and Shemiramoth and Jehiel and Mattithiah and Eliab and Benaiah and Obed-Edom and Jeiel, with instruments of harps and with lyres; and Asaph with cymbals sounding aloud.
pieces: Asaph was the leader, and next to him was Zechariah. Jeiel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Mattithiah, Eliab, Benaiah, Obed-Edom and Jeiel played harps and lyres, and Asaph sounded the cymbals.

L.5: Asaph [was] the chief, and second to him Zechariah; Jeiel and Shemiramoth and Jehiel and Mattithiah and Eliab and Benaiah and Obed-Edom and Jeiel [were] with instruments, harps and lyres; and Asaph [was] sounding aloud with cymbals.

R.5: Asaph was in charge, and Zechariah was second to him. Jeiel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Mattithiah, Eliab, Benaiah, Obed-Edom and Jeiel played harps and lyres. Asaph played the cymbals loudly.

decisions.reason: Asaph and these Levites were among the singers chosen to go up with the ark (15:17-21), where Asaph also plays bronze cymbals (15:19). Asaph is the singer named in the titles of Psalms 50 and 73-83.

decisions.choice: Jeiel: the first of the two, perhaps the Jaaziel of 15:18
decisions.reason: Jeiel is named twice in this list. In the list of 15:18 the name in this place is Jaaziel (Aziel in 15:20), so the first Jeiel may be a copying change from that name. The Hebrew text is kept as it stands.

The lyre (kinnor) was the small stringed instrument David played (1 Samuel 16:23); the harp (nevel) was a larger stringed instrument. Cymbals were struck metal plates, used to sound out loudly (15:19).

decisions.choice: sounding aloud: Asaph led with the cymbals
decisions.reason: The participle describes Asaph's ongoing part: he made the cymbals heard, perhaps to give the beat or to mark the start of the songs, as the chief musician.
"With instruments of harps and with lyres" means they played them; Balanced and Readable say so.

records.source: וּבְנָיָ֥הוּ וְיַחֲזִיאֵ֖ל הַכֹּהֲנִ֑ים בַּחֲצֹצְר֣וֹת תָּמִ֔יד לִפְנֵ֖י אֲר֥וֹן בְּרִית־הָאֱלֹהִֽים׃
records.gloss: And Benaiah and Jahaziel the priests with trumpets continually before [the] ark of [the] covenant of the God.
pieces: The priests Benaiah and Jahaziel blew trumpets regularly before the ark of the covenant of God.

L.6: And Benaiah and Jahaziel the priests [were] with trumpets continually before the ark of the covenant of God.

R.6: Benaiah and Jahaziel, who were priests, blew trumpets at set times in front of the ark of God's covenant.

decisions.reason: The silver trumpets were blown by the priests (Numbers 10:8-10), and priests blew them before the ark when it was brought up (15:24). This Benaiah is a priest, not the Levite Benaiah of verse 5.

decisions.choice: continually: regularly, at the set times
decisions.reason: The word (tamid) is used of what is done day by day without fail, like the daily offering (verse 40), not of something done without a break.
"With trumpets" means they blew them; Balanced and Readable supply the verb. Readable says "at set times" for "continually" (m2).

records.source: בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא אָ֣ז נָתַ֤ן דָּוִיד֙ בָּרֹ֔אשׁ לְהֹד֖וֹת לַיהוָ֑ה בְּיַד־אָסָ֖ף וְאֶחָֽיו׃פ
records.gloss: On the day the that, then appointed David at first to give thanks to Yahweh by [the] hand of Asaph and his brothers:
pieces: It was on that day that David first put Asaph and his fellow Levites in charge of giving thanks to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}:

L.7: On that day, then, David first appointed [the] giving of thanks to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} by the hand of Asaph and his brothers:

R.7: That was the day David first gave Asaph and his fellow Levites the work of thanking {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. This was their song of thanks:

decisions.choice: first: for the first time, or as the first task
decisions.reason: The phrase (barosh) is "at the head". It most likely means that on this day David first gave the Levites this service of thanks; it could also mean that thanksgiving was put first among their tasks, or that Asaph was put at the head of it.

decisions.choice: by the hand of Asaph: in Asaph's charge
decisions.reason: "By the hand of" names those through whom a task is done; the thanksgiving was given into the care of Asaph and his brothers, the Levites of verse 5.

decisions.choice: the song follows without a word of saying
decisions.reason: The Hebrew goes straight from this verse into the song of verses 8-36, without saying "and they sang". The song is the thanks David appointed for that day.
"His brothers" here means Asaph's fellow Levites, the singers named in verse 5, not only his brothers by birth. Literal keeps "brothers".

decisions.choice: This was their song of thanks
decisions.reason: Readable introduces the song so that young readers see that the poem which follows is the thanks of this verse (m3).

records.source: הוֹד֤וּ לַֽיהוָה֙ קִרְא֣וּ בִשְׁמ֔וֹ הוֹדִ֥יעוּ בָעַמִּ֖ים עֲלִילֹתָֽיו׃
records.gloss: Give thanks to Yahweh; call on his name; make known among the peoples his deeds.
pieces: Thank {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and call on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name; \q tell every people what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has done.

L.8: Give thanks to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; call on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name; \q make known among the peoples {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} deeds.

R.8: Thank {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! Pray to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} by name. \q Tell people everywhere what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has done.

decisions.choice: the song is drawn from three psalms
decisions.reason: The song of verses 8-36 is made of Psalm 105:1-15 (verses 8-22), most of Psalm 96 (verses 23-33), and Psalm 106:1 and 106:47-48 (verses 34-36). Its wording follows those psalms wherever the Hebrew is the same, and each verse names where the two differ. This verse is Psalm 105:1.

decisions.choice: the song is given as it was sung, not as a quotation
decisions.reason: Verse 7 leads straight into the song without a word of saying, so the song is set out on its own, not as someone's speech.

decisions.choice: call on his name: pray to him, or proclaim him
decisions.reason: To call on the name of the LORD is to pray to him by name, as Abraham did (Genesis 12:8); it can also mean to proclaim his name aloud. The next line, "make known", leans toward praise spoken before others.
Readable says what calling on the name means (m3), as at Psalm 105:1.

records.heading: David's song of thanks

records.source: שִׁ֤ירוּ לוֹ֙ זַמְּרוּ־ל֔וֹ שִׂ֖יחוּ בְּכָל־נִפְלְאֹתָֽיו׃
records.gloss: Sing to him, make music to him; tell of all his wonders.
pieces: Sing to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, play and sing {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} praise; \q talk of all the wonderful things {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has done.

L.9: Sing to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, make music to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; \q tell of all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} wonders.

R.9: Sing to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}! Make music for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}! \q Talk about all the amazing things {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has done.

decisions.reason: This line is Psalm 105:2, with the same Hebrew, and its wording here follows the psalm.
The verb (zimmer) is used of songs sung to the music of instruments, like the harps, lyres and cymbals of verse 5.
The word (nifla'ot) is used of the great acts of God at the exodus (Exodus 3:20).

records.source: הִֽתְהַֽלְלוּ֙ בְּשֵׁ֣ם קָדְשׁ֔וֹ יִשְׂמַ֕ח לֵ֖ב מְבַקְשֵׁ֥י יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: Boast in [the] name of his holiness; let it rejoice, [the] heart of those who seek Yahweh.
pieces: Take pride in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy name; \q let all who look to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} be glad at heart.

L.10: Glory in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy name; \q let the heart of those who seek {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} rejoice.

R.10: Be proud of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy name. \q Everyone who looks for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} should be glad.

decisions.reason: This line is Psalm 105:3, with the same Hebrew, and its wording here follows the psalm.
The verb (hithallel) is to boast. Here the boast is not in oneself but in the LORD (Psalm 34:3; Jeremiah 9:23).

decisions.choice: the name of his holiness: his holy name
decisions.reason: Hebrew often uses a noun ("of holiness") where other languages use an adjective; the name stands for God himself as he has made himself known.

decisions.choice: seek: turn to in prayer and worship
decisions.reason: To seek the LORD (biqqesh) is to come to him for help and to worship him, often at his sanctuary (Psalms 24:6; 27:8).

records.source: דִּרְשׁ֤וּ יְהוָה֙ וְעֻזּ֔וֹ בַּקְּשׁ֥וּ פָנָ֖יו תָּמִֽיד׃
records.gloss: Seek Yahweh and his strength; seek his face continually.
pieces: Turn to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} strength; \q come into {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} presence again and again.

L.11: Seek {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} strength; \q seek {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} face continually.

R.11: Turn to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and depend on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} strength. \q Never stop coming to worship {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.reason: This line is Psalm 105:4, with the same Hebrew, and its wording here follows the psalm.

decisions.choice: his strength: the strength he gives, or the ark
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean the strength that comes from God. In Psalms 78:61 and 132:8 "his strength" is a name for the ark, which fits this day, when the ark has just been brought to Jerusalem (verse 1).

decisions.choice: seek his face: come before him
decisions.reason: God's face is his presence; to seek it is to come before him in worship (Psalms 24:6; 27:8).

decisions.choice: come into his presence again and again (B); Never stop coming to worship him (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what seeking his face means (m3), as at Psalm 105:4.

records.source: זִכְר֗וּ נִפְלְאֹתָיו֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֔ה מֹפְתָ֖יו וּמִשְׁפְּטֵי־פִֽיהוּ׃
records.gloss: Remember his wonders which he has done, his signs and [the] judgments of his mouth,
pieces: Call to mind the wonders {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has worked, \q {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} signs, and the verdicts {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke,

L.12: Remember {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} wonders that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has done, \q {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} signs and the judgments of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mouth,

R.12: Remember the amazing things {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has done. \q Remember {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} miracles and the judgments {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} announced.

decisions.reason: This line is Psalm 105:5, with the same Hebrew, and its wording here follows the psalm.

decisions.choice: signs: acts that point to God's power
decisions.reason: The word (mofet) is a sign or portent, used of the plagues on Egypt (Exodus 7:3; 11:9).

decisions.choice: the judgments of his mouth: the sentences he pronounced
decisions.reason: God spoke his judgments and they were carried out, as when he promised to bring Israel out of Egypt "with great judgments" (Exodus 6:6; 7:4).
Verse 13 names those who are called to remember, so the sentence runs on into the next verse.

records.source: זֶ֚רַע יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל עַבְדּ֔וֹ בְּנֵ֥י יַעֲקֹ֖ב בְּחִירָֽיו׃
records.gloss: offspring of Israel his servant, sons of Jacob, his chosen ones.
pieces: you descendants of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servant Israel, \q you children of Jacob, the ones {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} chose.

L.13: you offspring of Israel {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servant, \q you sons of Jacob, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} chosen ones.

R.13: Do this, you who come from Israel, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servant, \q you descendants of Jacob, whom {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} chose.

decisions.reason: Psalm 105:6 reads "offspring of Abraham his servant". Here the line reads "offspring of Israel his servant", so both halves of the verse name the same ancestor, Jacob, who was also called Israel (Genesis 32:29). The rest of the wording follows the psalm.

decisions.choice: his servant: Israel; his chosen ones: Jacob's children
decisions.reason: "His servant" stands beside Israel, and "his chosen ones" (plural) beside the sons of Jacob. The people are addressed through their ancestor.
"Sons of Jacob" means the whole people descended from him, so Balanced and Readable say "children", as at Psalm 105:6; Literal keeps "sons".
Readable ended verse 12 with a full stop, so it links the people addressed here to the commands before them.

records.source: ה֚וּא יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ בְּכָל־הָאָ֖רֶץ מִשְׁפָּטָֽיו׃
records.gloss: He [is] Yahweh our God; in all the earth [are] his judgments.
pieces: He, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, is our God; \q {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} rulings reach the whole earth.

L.14: He [is] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God; \q in all the earth [are] {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} judgments.

R.14: He is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, our God. \q He judges what happens everywhere on earth.

decisions.reason: This line is Psalm 105:7, with the same Hebrew, and its wording here follows the psalm.
The pronoun stands first for emphasis: this God who did all these things is the LORD, Israel's own God.

decisions.choice: his judgments in all the earth
decisions.reason: The God of one people is judge of every nation; he ruled over the kings of the nations for his people's sake (verse 21).

records.source: זִכְר֤וּ לְעוֹלָם֙ בְּרִית֔וֹ דָּבָ֥ר צִוָּ֖ה לְאֶ֥לֶף דּֽוֹר׃
records.gloss: Remember forever his covenant, [the] word he commanded for a thousand generation[s],
pieces: Keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} covenant in mind forever, \q the promise {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} laid down for a thousand generations,

L.15: Remember {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} covenant forever, \q the word {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} commanded for a thousand generations,

R.15: Never forget {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} covenant, \q the promise {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made to last for a thousand generations.

decisions.reason: Psalm 105:8 reads "He remembers his covenant forever": God keeps his promise. Here the verb is a command to the people, "Remember his covenant forever", like "remember" in verse 12. The rest of the line is the same as the psalm, and its wording follows the psalm's.

decisions.choice: the word he commanded for a thousand generations: a promise without end
decisions.reason: The "word" is the promise of the covenant, set in place by God's command. "A thousand generations" means for all time (Deuteronomy 7:9).

decisions.choice: remember: keep in mind and live by it
decisions.reason: To remember the covenant is not only to recall it but to keep faith with it, as God himself does (Exodus 2:24; Psalm 105:8).

decisions.choice: Keep in mind (B); Never forget (R); the promise
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the wording of Psalm 105:8 turned into a command, and say what the word is (m2).

decisions.reason: A covenant was "cut", perhaps from the animals cut in two when it was made, as in Genesis 15:9-18.

decisions.choice: the covenant with Abraham and the oath to Isaac
decisions.reason: God made his covenant with Abraham and promised him the land (Genesis 15:18; 17:7-8), swore by himself to bless him (Genesis 22:16-18), and confirmed the oath to Isaac (Genesis 26:3-4).

decisions.reason: This line is Psalm 105:10, with the same Hebrew, and its wording here follows the psalm.

decisions.reason: God renewed the promise of the land to Jacob at Bethel (Genesis 28:13-15; 35:11-12), where he also confirmed the name Israel (Genesis 35:10). The two names here are the same man.
The word (choq) is something laid down that does not change. God bound himself to his promise as firmly as a law.

decisions.choice: set it in place (B); made it a firm law (R)
decisions.reason: The verb (he'emid) is to make something stand; Balanced and Readable keep that picture of firmness, as at Psalm 105:10.

decisions.reason: This line is Psalm 105:11, with the same Hebrew, and its wording here follows the psalm.
God promised Canaan to Abraham and his offspring (Genesis 12:7; 13:15; 17:8) and to Jacob (Genesis 28:13).
"To you" is singular, spoken to each of the fathers; "your inheritance" is plural, the share of the whole people descended from them.

decisions.choice: portion: a share marked out with a line
decisions.reason: The word (chevel) is a measuring cord, and then the plot of land measured with it (Deuteronomy 32:9).
Readable starts a new sentence and names the speaker, God.

records.source: בִּֽהְיֽוֹתְכֶם֙ מְתֵ֣י מִסְפָּ֔ר כִּמְעַ֖ט וְגָרִ֥ים בָּֽהּ׃

L.19: When you were men of [small] number, \q very few, and sojourners in it,

R.19: At that time there were only a few of you. \q You were foreigners living in Canaan.

decisions.reason: Psalm 105:12 reads "when they were". Here the singers say "when you were", speaking to the people of their own day as if they had been there with their ancestors. The next verse goes back to "they", as the psalm has it. The rest of the wording follows the psalm.

decisions.choice: men of number: few, easily counted
decisions.reason: People who can be counted are few (Genesis 34:30; Deuteronomy 26:5, "few in number"). "Like a few" makes it stronger: very few indeed.

decisions.choice: sojourners: foreigners living in the land
decisions.reason: A sojourner (ger) lived in a land without owning it, under others' protection. Abraham called himself one in Canaan (Genesis 23:4).

decisions.choice: the "when" clause goes with what follows
decisions.reason: As in Psalm 105:12, the clause is taken with verse 21: while they were few and wandering, God protected them.
Readable names the land that "it" refers to, as at Psalm 105:12; it keeps the psalm's wording for the sojourners.

L.20: and they went about from nation to nation, \q and from a kingdom to another people,

R.20: They wandered from one country to another, \q from one kingdom to the next.

decisions.reason: This line is Psalm 105:13, and its wording follows the psalm. Chronicles adds "and" before "from a kingdom", which does not change the sense. After "you" in verse 19, the line returns to "they", the ancestors.

Abraham went from Haran to Canaan and down to Egypt (Genesis 12:4-10) and lived in Gerar (Genesis 20:1); Isaac lived in Gerar (Genesis 26:6); Jacob went to Haran and back (Genesis 28-31) and at last to Egypt (Genesis 46:1-7).

decisions.choice: went about: walked here and there
decisions.reason: The verb (hithallekh) is to go to and fro, a life on the move without a land of one's own.

records.source: לֹא־הִנִּ֤יחַ לְאִישׁ֙ לְעָשְׁקָ֔ם וַיּ֥וֹכַח עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם מְלָכִֽים׃

decisions.reason: Psalm 105:14 has 'adam, "a human being", where Chronicles has 'ish, "a man"; both mean "anyone" here, and the wording follows the psalm.

decisions.choice: kings rebuked for the fathers' sake
decisions.reason: God struck Pharaoh because of Sarah (Genesis 12:17), warned Abimelech king of Gerar in a dream (Genesis 20:3-7), and Abimelech later forbade anyone to harm Isaac (Genesis 26:11).
Readable starts a new sentence, so it names God, and it introduces the words of verse 22 as his, as at Psalm 105:14.

R.22: "Do not harm the people I have set apart for {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}}. \q Do not hurt {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} prophets."

decisions.choice: Psalm 105:15: the end of the psalm's lines
decisions.reason: This line is Psalm 105:15, and its wording follows the psalm. The song takes no more from Psalm 105; it goes on with Psalm 96 in verse 23.

decisions.choice: my anointed ones: the fathers, set apart by God
decisions.reason: Kings and priests were anointed with oil. The fathers never were, but they were chosen and set apart by God as if anointed.
God calls Abraham a prophet who will pray for Abimelech (Genesis 20:7).

decisions.choice: the people I have set apart for myself
decisions.reason: Readable says what "anointed" means here (m2), as at Psalm 105:15.

R.23: Everyone on earth, sing to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! \q Tell the good news every day: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saves!

decisions.reason: The song now takes up Psalm 96, which it follows to verse 33. This verse joins the second half of Psalm 96:1 ("sing to the LORD, all the earth") to the second half of Psalm 96:2 ("bear news from day to day of his salvation"). It leaves out "Sing to the LORD a new song" and "Sing to the LORD, bless his name". The wording of each half follows the psalm.

decisions.choice: all the earth: everyone on earth
decisions.reason: The whole earth is called on, that is, all its peoples (verses 24, 28, 31), not Israel only.
The verb (basar) is to bring news, usually good news, as in Isaiah 40:9 and 52:7.

decisions.reason: This line is Psalm 96:3, and its wording follows the psalm.
The word (kavod) is literally weight, and so the greatness and splendor of God that deserves honor.
The word (nifla'ot) is used of God's great acts, such as the rescue from Egypt (Exodus 3:20; Psalm 78:4).

R.25: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is great, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} deserves all our praise. \q People should honor and fear {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} far more than any so-called god.

decisions.reason: This line is Psalm 96:4, and its wording follows the psalm. Chronicles adds "and" before "to be feared", which changes nothing in the sense.

decisions.choice: to be feared: to be held in awe
decisions.reason: The form (nora') means one who is to be feared, that is, honored with awe and reverence (Psalm 47:3).
The other gods are not real rivals; the next verse says what they are.
Readable prepares for verse 26, which says these gods are nothing (m3), as at Psalm 96:4.

R.26: The gods of the other nations are only idols. They are nothing! \q But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made the sky above us.

decisions.reason: This line is Psalm 96:5, and its wording follows the psalm.
The word ('elilim) means worthless things and is used for idols. It sounds like the word for gods ('elohim), a play on words: the gods of the peoples are no-gods (Isaiah 2:8; Leviticus 19:4).

decisions.choice: made the heavens: the Creator above the gods
decisions.reason: The nations' gods were made by people; the LORD made the sky, where the nations placed their gods. That is the proof of who is God (Psalm 115:3-4).

The ark had no temple yet, only the tent David pitched (verse 1), and the joy of the day is part of what surrounds God. The first half of the line is the same as the psalm, and the wording follows it.

decisions.choice: splendor and majesty: the glory of a king
decisions.reason: The pair (hod, hadar) is used of a king's splendor (Psalms 21:6; 45:4). Here they stand before the LORD like attendants at his throne.

decisions.choice: his place: where God dwells among his people
decisions.reason: The word (maqom) is the ordinary word for a place, and is used of the place God chooses for his name (Deuteronomy 12:5) and of the place prepared for the ark (15:1, 3).

decisions.choice: the place where he dwells (B); the place where he lives (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "his place" is: God's dwelling. Readable keeps the words of Psalm 96:6.

The verb (yahav) is simply "give"; giving glory and strength to God is acknowledging that they are his.
Verses 28-29 echo Psalm 29:1-2, where the same call is made to the heavenly beings; here it goes out to the families of all the peoples (Genesis 12:3).

decisions.reason: The verse joins Psalm 96:8 to the first half of Psalm 96:9. Where the psalm says "come into his courts", the courts of the temple, Chronicles says "come before him", since there was no temple yet. The rest of the wording follows the psalm.

decisions.reason: The word (minchah) is a gift, the tribute brought to a king (2 Samuel 8:2), and the grain offering of the sanctuary (Leviticus 2:1). The nations come like subjects to their King.

decisions.choice: the splendor of holiness: God's holy splendor
decisions.reason: The phrase (hadrat qodesh) may describe God's holy splendor, the setting of the worship, or the holy attire of those who worship (as in Psalm 29:2; 2 Chronicles 20:21).

decisions.choice: come into his presence (B); come to him (R)
decisions.reason: "Come before him" means coming into his presence; Balanced says so to avoid repeating "before" in the next line.

decisions.reason: The verse joins the second half of Psalm 96:9 ("tremble before him, all the earth") to Psalm 96:10's "the world is established; it will not be shaken". The psalm's "Say among the nations, The LORD reigns" comes in the next verse, and its "He will judge the peoples with uprightness" is not repeated. The wording follows the psalm.
The verb (chil) is to writhe or tremble, here in awe before the King.

Readable names who made the world firm, which the passive verb implies, as at Psalm 96:10.

decisions.reason: The first half is Psalm 96:11a. The second half is the cry of Psalm 96:10a, "The LORD reigns!", moved here and introduced with "and let them say" where the psalm has "Say". The wording follows the psalm.

decisions.choice: let them say: let it be said

The verb (malak) with the LORD as subject is the cry of Psalms 93, 96, 97 and 99. The same form was shouted when a new king took the throne (2 Samuel 15:10; 2 Kings 9:13), so it may also mean "has become King".

decisions.choice: is King; let it be told (B); Let people tell (R)
decisions.reason: As at Psalm 96:10, Balanced and Readable say "is King"; Literal keeps "reigns". They turn "let them say" into words that leave the subject general (m2).

pieces: Let the sea thunder with all that lives in it; \q let the fields and everything in them celebrate.

decisions.reason: The verse joins the end of Psalm 96:11 to the start of Psalm 96:12, and its wording follows the psalm. Chronicles spells the verb "exult" and the word "field" a little differently from the psalm; the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: its fullness: all that fills the sea
decisions.reason: The word (melo') is what fills something; here the creatures of the sea (Psalm 24:1).
The sea is often a picture of chaos and threat (Psalm 93:3-4); here even the sea thunders in praise of its King.

records.gloss: Then they will shout for joy, [the] trees of the forest, before Yahweh, for he comes to judge the earth.
pieces: Then the trees of the woods will cry out with joy \q in the presence of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is on the way to judge the earth.

L.33: Then the trees of the forest will shout for joy \q before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} comes to judge the earth.

R.33: Then the trees in the forest will sing for joy \q in the presence of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is coming to rule the earth as judge.

decisions.reason: Psalm 96:12-13 reads "all the trees of the forest" and "for he comes, for he comes to judge the earth", and goes on "He will judge the world with righteousness and the peoples with his faithfulness". Chronicles has "the trees" without "all", says "for he comes" once, and ends the line at "to judge the earth". The wording follows the psalm.

decisions.choice: the trees shout for joy: creation welcomes its King
decisions.reason: The poem pictures the whole creation, sky, sea, field and forest, celebrating the King's coming, as in Isaiah 55:12.

decisions.choice: judge: rule and set things right
decisions.reason: The verb (shafat) means more than passing sentence: it is to govern and to put wrongs right. For a world under wrong, the coming of this Judge is good news, and creation sings.

decisions.choice: comes: is coming, or has come
decisions.reason: The form can mean "he has come" or "he is coming". On this day the ark, the sign of his presence, has come into Jerusalem; the joy of creation looks forward to his coming to judge.

records.gloss: Give thanks to Yahweh, for [he is] good, for to forever [is] his loyal love.
pieces: Give {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} thanks, for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is good; \q {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} loyal love lasts forever.

L.34: Give thanks to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for [{{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is] good, \q for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} loyal love [is] forever.

R.34: Thank {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is good! \q His faithful love lasts forever.

decisions.reason: The song closes with lines from Psalm 106. This verse is Psalm 106:1 without its opening "Praise Yah", and its wording follows the psalm. The same words open Psalms 107, 118 and 136 and are sung again in 2 Chronicles 5:13 and Ezra 3:11; verse 41 names them as the words of the thanks the Levites gave.
The word (chesed) is the love that keeps faith, God's commitment to his people that does not give up.

This line is Psalm 106:1, so its wording is kept the same as the psalm's, which has "loyal love" at Literal and Balanced and "faithful love" at Readable; elsewhere in these books chesed is "steadfast love" at Literal and "faithful love" at Balanced, as at 2 Samuel 22:51.

records.source: וְאִמְר֕וּ הוֹשִׁיעֵ֨נוּ֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׁעֵ֔נוּ וְקַבְּצֵ֥נוּ וְהַצִּילֵ֖נוּ מִן־הַגּוֹיִ֑ם לְהֹדוֹת֙ לְשֵׁ֣ם קָדְשֶׁ֔ךָ לְהִשְׁתַּבֵּ֖חַ בִּתְהִלָּתֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: And say, Save us, God of our salvation, and gather us and deliver us from the nations, to give thanks to [the] name of your holiness, to boast in your praise.
pieces: Say also, "Rescue us, God our Savior; \q gather us and deliver us from among the nations, \q so that we may thank {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} holy name and make our boast in praising {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."

L.35: And say, "Save us, God of our salvation, \q and gather us and deliver us from the nations, \q to give thanks to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} holy name, to glory in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} praise."

R.35: Say also, "Save us, God our Savior! \q Gather us and rescue us from the other nations. \q Then we will thank {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, the holy God, and proudly sing {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} praise."

decisions.choice: Psalm 106:47, with "Say", "God of our salvation" and "deliver us"
decisions.reason: Psalm 106:47 begins "Save us, LORD our God, and gather us from the nations". Here the line begins with a call to the singers, "And say"; God is called "God of our salvation"; and "and deliver us" is added. The rest follows the psalm and its wording.

The prayer is for a people scattered among the nations. The law promised that if they returned to the LORD he would gather them from all the peoples (Deuteronomy 30:3-4). Sung on the day the ark came home, it asks God to bring all his people home as well.
The verb (hishtabbeach) is to boast or take pride; their boast will be in praising God.
"God of our salvation" is the God who saves us; Balanced and Readable say "God our Savior". Balanced keeps the psalm's "Rescue us" for the first verb and uses "deliver" for the added one.
Readable says "Gather us" here, where Psalm 106:47 has "Bring us back home", because in this song the prayer is not tied to a return from exile.

records.source: בָּר֤וּךְ יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מִן־הָעוֹלָ֖ם וְעַ֣ד הָעֹלָ֑ם וַיֹּאמְר֤וּ כָל־הָעָם֙ אָמֵ֔ן וְהַלֵּ֖ל לַֽיהוָֽה׃פ
records.gloss: Blessed [be] Yahweh, [the] God of Israel, from the everlasting and until the everlasting. And said all the people, Amen, and praise to Yahweh.
pieces: May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, be blessed from ages past to ages to come! \q Then all the people said, "Amen!" and praised {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.36: Blessed [be] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting! \q And all the people said, "Amen," and praised {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.36: Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel! He has always been worthy of praise, and always will be. \q Then all the people said, "Amen!" and they praised {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: Psalm 106:48, with the people's answer told as what they did
decisions.reason: The first half is Psalm 106:48, and its wording follows the psalm. The psalm ends "And let all the people say, Amen. Praise Yah"; here the narrator says what the people did: they said "Amen" and praised the LORD.

decisions.choice: from everlasting to everlasting: for all time, past and future
decisions.reason: The word ('olam) is the farthest time, before or ahead; the pair means always (Psalms 41:14; 90:2).
Amen ('amen) is a word of agreement: "it is true, so be it". The people make the song their own.

decisions.choice: and praised: a verb form that continues the narrative
decisions.reason: The verb "praise" here is a form without person or tense that carries on from "they said": the people praised the LORD.

records.source: וַיַּֽעֲזָב־שָׁ֗ם לִפְנֵי֙ אֲר֣וֹן בְּרִית־יְהוָ֔ה לְאָסָ֖ף וּלְאֶחָ֑יו לְשָׁרֵ֞ת לִפְנֵ֧י הָאָר֛וֹן תָּמִ֖יד לִדְבַר־י֥וֹם בְּיוֹמֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And he left there before [the] ark of [the] covenant of Yahweh Asaph and his brothers, to minister before the ark continually, as [the] matter of a day in its day.
pieces: So David left Asaph and his fellow Levites there before the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, to serve before the ark regularly, as each day's work required.

L.37: And he left there, before the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, Asaph and his brothers, to minister before the ark continually, as each day's matter [required] on its day.

R.37: David left Asaph and his fellow Levites there in front of the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s covenant. They were to serve there every day, doing what each day required.

decisions.reason: The subject of "left" is David, who appointed the Levites in verses 4 and 7. The same verb governs verses 38-39: he left Asaph at the ark in Jerusalem, and Zadok and the priests at Gibeon.

decisions.choice: the matter of a day in its day: each day's duty
decisions.reason: The phrase means the work set for each day, done on that day (Exodus 5:13; Ezra 3:4). The Levites' song before the ark became a daily service.

From now until the temple is built, worship is divided: the ark is in David's tent in Jerusalem, with the singers (verses 37-38), while the tabernacle and its altar stay at Gibeon, with the priests (verses 39-42).
Balanced and Readable name David (m1) and, as in verse 7, call Asaph's "brothers" his fellow Levites.

records.heading: Worship before the ark and at Gibeon

records.source: וְעֹבֵ֥ד אֱדֹ֛ם וַאֲחֵיהֶ֖ם שִׁשִּׁ֣ים וּשְׁמוֹנָ֑ה וְעֹבֵ֨ד אֱדֹ֧ם בֶּן־יְדִית֛וּן וְחֹסָ֖ה לְשֹׁעֲרִֽים׃
records.gloss: And Obed-Edom and their brothers, sixty and eight; and Obed-Edom [the] son of Jedithun and Hosah to gatekeepers.
pieces: He also left Obed-Edom and their relatives, sixty-eight in all, and Obed-Edom son of Jeduthun and Hosah as gatekeepers.

L.38: And [he left] Obed-Edom and their brothers, sixty-eight; and Obed-Edom son of Jeduthun and Hosah as gatekeepers.

R.38: Obed-Edom and sixty-eight of their relatives also stayed there. Obed-Edom son of Jeduthun and Hosah were gatekeepers.

decisions.choice: their brothers: a name may be missing
decisions.reason: "Their" is plural though only Obed-Edom has been named, so a second name, perhaps Hosah, may have dropped out in copying. The Hebrew text is kept as it stands.

decisions.choice: Obed-Edom son of Jeduthun: perhaps the same man
decisions.reason: Obed-Edom is named twice. He may be one man, given here his father's name and his task, or two men of that name. An Obed-Edom was among the musicians (verse 5; 15:21) and also among the gatekeepers (15:18, 24; 26:4-8). This Jeduthun may not be the singer of verse 41.

decisions.choice: gatekeepers: guards of the sanctuary entrances
decisions.reason: The gatekeepers (sho'arim) were Levites who kept watch at the entrances of the holy place (9:17-27).
The written text here spells the name a little differently (Jedithun); every level uses the usual form, Jeduthun, as the data gives it.

records.source: וְאֵ֣ת׀צָד֣וֹק הַכֹּהֵ֗ן וְאֶחָיו֙ הַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים לִפְנֵ֖י מִשְׁכַּ֣ן יְהוָ֑ה בַּבָּמָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּגִבְעֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: And Zadok the priest and his brothers the priests before [the] tabernacle of Yahweh at the high place that [was] at Gibeon,
pieces: He left the priest Zadok and his fellow priests at the high place in Gibeon, before the tabernacle of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}},

L.39: And [he left] Zadok the priest and his brothers the priests before the tabernacle of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} at the high place that [was] at Gibeon,

R.39: David left Zadok the priest and the other priests in front of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s tabernacle at the hilltop shrine in Gibeon.

decisions.reason: The Hebrew marks Zadok as an object, so David's "left" in verse 37 still governs: he left Zadok and the priests at Gibeon. The sentence runs on into verse 40.
The tabernacle made under Moses, with its bronze altar, stood at Gibeon (21:29; 2 Chronicles 1:3-6). Solomon offered sacrifices there at the start of his reign (1 Kings 3:4).

decisions.choice: high place: a place of worship on a height
decisions.reason: A high place (bamah) was a shrine on a hill. Many high places were later condemned, but this one held the LORD's own tabernacle and altar, and the law's offerings were made there (verse 40).
Zadok was one of David's two chief priests, with Abiathar (15:11; 2 Samuel 8:17); he later anointed Solomon (1 Kings 1:39).
Readable says "hilltop shrine" for "high place", as elsewhere in these books.

records.source: לְֽהַעֲלוֹת֩ עֹל֨וֹת לַיהוָ֜ה עַל־מִזְבַּ֧ח הָעֹלָ֛ה תָּמִ֖יד לַבֹּ֣קֶר וְלָעָ֑רֶב וּלְכָל־הַכָּתוּב֙ בְּתוֹרַ֣ת יְהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוָּ֖ה עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: to offer up burnt offerings to Yahweh on [the] altar of the burnt offering continually, morning and evening, and according to all that [is] written in [the] law of Yahweh which he commanded upon Israel.
pieces: to offer burnt offerings to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} on the altar of burnt offering regularly, morning and evening, according to all that is written in the law of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} laid down for Israel.

L.40: to offer burnt offerings to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} on the altar of burnt offering continually, morning and evening, and according to all that is written in the law of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} commanded Israel.

R.40: They were to offer burnt offerings to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} on the altar of burnt offering every morning and every evening. They were to do all that is written in the law that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave Israel to obey.

decisions.choice: the daily burnt offering, morning and evening
decisions.reason: The law commanded a lamb to be offered as a burnt offering each morning and each evening (Exodus 29:38-42; Numbers 28:3-8). This regular offering went on at the altar at Gibeon.

decisions.choice: the law of the LORD: the written law given through Moses
decisions.reason: The law (torah) here is the written instruction of the LORD, as "written" shows (2 Chronicles 23:18; 31:3).

decisions.choice: according to all that is written
decisions.reason: Chronicles stresses that worship was done as God's law prescribed. The first attempt to move the ark failed because it was not done in the way the law laid down (15:13-15).
The one who commanded is the LORD, whose law it is.

decisions.choice: every morning and every evening; gave Israel to obey
decisions.reason: Readable says "every" for "continually" and turns "which he commanded Israel" into plain words.

records.source: וְעִמָּהֶם֙ הֵימָ֣ן וִֽידוּת֔וּן וּשְׁאָר֙ הַבְּרוּרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר נִקְּב֖וּ בְּשֵׁמ֑וֹת לְהֹדוֹת֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה כִּ֥י לְעוֹלָ֖ם חַסְדּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And with them Heman and Jeduthun and [the] rest of the chosen [ones] who were designated by names, to give thanks to Yahweh, for to forever [is] his loyal love.
pieces: With them were Heman and Jeduthun and the rest of those chosen and named one by one to give thanks to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} loyal love lasts forever.

L.41: And with them [were] Heman and Jeduthun and the rest of the chosen [men] who were designated by name, to give thanks to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} loyal love [is] forever.

R.41: Heman and Jeduthun were with them, along with the others who had been chosen by name for this work. Their task was to thank {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, because {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} faithful love lasts forever.

decisions.choice: with them: with Zadok and the priests at Gibeon
decisions.reason: "Them" are the priests of verse 39. So Heman and Jeduthun led the song at Gibeon, while Asaph led it before the ark in Jerusalem (verse 37).
Heman and Jeduthun (probably the Ethan of 15:17, 19) were, with Asaph, the heads of the Levite singers (25:1-6). Their names stand in the titles of Psalms 39, 62, 77 and 88.

decisions.choice: for his loyal love is forever: the refrain of verse 34
decisions.reason: These are the words of verse 34 (Psalm 106:1), the refrain of Israel's thanksgiving (2 Chronicles 5:13; 7:6). They may give the reason for the thanks or the very words that were sung.

decisions.choice: designated by names: named one by one
decisions.reason: Each singer was appointed by name, not chosen at random (12:32).

As in verse 34, the refrain keeps the wording of Psalm 106:1, "loyal love" at Literal and Balanced and "faithful love" at Readable, rather than the "steadfast love / faithful love" used for chesed elsewhere in these books (17:13; 19:2), so that the refrain reads the same wherever it is sung.

records.source: וְעִמָּהֶם֩ הֵימָ֨ן וִֽידוּת֜וּן חֲצֹצְר֤וֹת וּמְצִלְתַּ֨יִם֙ לְמַשְׁמִיעִ֔ים וּכְלֵ֖י שִׁ֣יר הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וּבְנֵ֥י יְדוּת֖וּן לַשָּֽׁעַר׃
records.gloss: And with them Heman and Jeduthun, trumpets and cymbals for those sounding aloud and instruments of [the] song of the God; and [the] sons of Jeduthun at the gate.
pieces: Heman and Jeduthun had with them trumpets and cymbals for the players to sound, and the instruments for the song of God. The sons of Jeduthun were at the gate.

L.42: And with them [were] Heman and Jeduthun, [with] trumpets and cymbals for those sounding aloud, and instruments for the song of God; and the sons of Jeduthun [were] at the gate.

R.42: Heman and Jeduthun had trumpets and cymbals for the musicians to play, and the other instruments used to sing to God. The sons of Jeduthun guarded the gate.

decisions.reason: The words "with them Heman and Jeduthun" repeat the start of verse 41. The repeat may have come in by copying; read as it stands, it says that these two leaders had the instruments in their charge.

decisions.choice: instruments of the song of God: instruments for sacred song
decisions.reason: The phrase means the instruments used for the songs sung to God, like "the instruments of the song of the LORD" that David made (2 Chronicles 7:6).

decisions.choice: the sons of Jeduthun at the gate: gatekeepers at Gibeon
decisions.reason: Some of Jeduthun's family served as gatekeepers, as Obed-Edom son of Jeduthun did in Jerusalem (verse 38).
Balanced and Readable say that the two leaders had the instruments, which the verbless Hebrew implies.

records.source: וַיֵּלְכ֥וּ כָל־הָעָ֖ם אִ֣ישׁ לְבֵית֑וֹ וַיִּסֹּ֥ב דָּוִ֖יד לְבָרֵ֥ךְ אֶת־בֵּיתֽוֹ׃פ
records.gloss: And went all the people, each to his house; and turned David to bless his house.
pieces: Then all the people went home, each to {{gender:their|his}} own house, and David turned back to bless his household.

L.43: And all the people went, each to {{gender:their|his}} house, and David turned to bless his household.

R.43: Then everyone went home. David also went home to bless his family.

decisions.reason: The verse is the end of 2 Samuel 6:19 and the start of 6:20, and its wording follows that passage. Samuel says David "returned" (shuv); Chronicles says he "turned" (savav). Chronicles does not go on to tell of Michal's scorn, which it has touched on already (15:29).

decisions.choice: bless his house: bless his household
decisions.reason: "House" here means the people of the house, David's family and servants. As he had blessed the people (verse 2), he went to bless his own household.
The people are men and women (verse 3), so the inclusive form is the default and "his" the alternative, as at 2 Samuel 6:19. Readable says "everyone", which needs no setting.
